quick: 0.1% three times daily, or 0.3% once daily (eye drops)
Avoid in late pregnancy (NSAID class); use only if clearly needed
Caution; systemic exposure is very low
Not relevant for topical ophthalmic use
summary: Nepafenac is a topical ophthalmic NSAID prodrug used to treat pain and inflammation associated with cataract surgery. After corneal penetration it is converted to amfenac, which inhibits cyclooxygenase and prostaglandin production. It carries class warnings for increased bleeding of ocular tissues, delayed wound healing, and corneal adverse effects (keratitis), and is contraindicated in patients hypersensitive to NSAIDs.
indications: Treatment of pain and inflammation associated with cataract surgery

dosage.c: Pain and inflammation after cataract surgery (0.3%)
dosage.d: One drop to the affected eye once daily, starting 1 day before surgery
dosage.t: Once daily through the first 2 weeks postoperatively
dosage.n: Give an additional drop 30-120 minutes before surgery

dosage.c: Pain and inflammation after cataract surgery (0.1%)
dosage.d: One drop to the affected eye three times daily, starting 1 day before surgery
dosage.t: Three times daily through the first 2 weeks postoperatively
dosage.n: Continue on the day of surgery and for 2 weeks after

admin: Instill one drop into the affected eye(s) as directed; avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface
If more than one topical eye medication is used, separate doses by at least 5 minutes
moa: After topical ocular dosing, nepafenac penetrates the cornea and is converted by ocular tissue hydrolases to amfenac, an NSAID. Nepafenac and amfenac inhibit prostaglandin H synthase (cyclooxygenase), the enzyme required for prostaglandin production, thereby reducing ocular pain and inflammation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to nepafenac or any formulation ingredient
relative: Known bleeding tendency or concurrent agents prolonging bleeding time
Complicated ocular surgery, corneal denervation, ocular surface disease (e.g., dry eye), diabetes mellitus, repeated surgeries within a short period (increased corneal risk)

preg: As an NSAID, avoid use during late pregnancy (around 30 weeks gestation onward) because of the risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus; systemic exposure from ophthalmic dosing is very low. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether topical ocular nepafenac is excreted in human milk; systemic exposure is minimal. Exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed; systemic absorption after topical ocular use is minimal.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed; systemic absorption after topical ocular use is minimal.

moderate: Topical or systemic agents that prolong bleeding time (increased ocular bleeding risk)
Concurrent topical corticosteroids (additive delayed corneal healing)
minor: Other topical ophthalmic NSAIDs (additive corneal effects)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor intraocular pressure and corneal status clinically

monitoring: Corneal status and signs of breakdown, especially in at-risk patients
Signs of ocular bleeding during and after surgery
counsel: Shake well and instill drops exactly as directed before and after surgery
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
Remove contact lenses before use and wait as advised before reinserting
Report eye pain, redness, increasing visual blurring, or discharge promptly
Separate different eye drops by at least 5 minutes
pk: Anti-inflammatory effect develops over the perioperative dosing period
Plasma nepafenac ~0.5 hour, amfenac ~0.75 hour (very low systemic levels)
Short systemic half-life; converted in ocular tissue to amfenac
0.3% supports once-daily dosing; 0.1% dosed three times daily
Store at 2-25 C (36-77 F); protect from light
pearls: Prodrug activated in the cornea to amfenac, giving good intraocular NSAID penetration
Watch for corneal complications in patients with ocular surface disease, diabetes, or repeated/complicated surgery
Use cautiously with corticosteroids - additive delay in corneal healing
0.3% is a convenient once-daily formulation versus 0.1% three times daily
missed: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Topical ophthalmic overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity given minimal absorption. Accidental ingestion of the contents should be managed by drinking fluids to dilute; provide supportive care. Excessive ocular application can be flushed from the eye(s) with lukewarm water.
